The following performance reviews are maintained in the employee's permanent personnel file. Reviews are written annually by the supervisor and reviewed by the Human Resources department. Each review reflects the employee's performance during the preceding calendar year.

**Performance Review — Review Period: 2015-01-01 to 2015-12-31**
**Review Date:** 2016-02-18
**Reviewer:** Director of Collections
**Overall Rating:** Meets Expectations

Clara continues to perform her duties as Registrar with accuracy and attention to detail. During this review period, she managed the annual inventory of the permanent collection, completing the count of 4,312 objects with only three minor discrepancies, all of which were resolved and documented. She also coordinated the loan agreements for two traveling exhibitions, working with external institutions to ensure that condition reports and insurance documentation were completed on schedule.

Her recordkeeping practices remain consistent, and she has demonstrated a strong working knowledge of the collections management database. Clara is encouraged to take a more active role in the development of departmental procedures, particularly in the area of shipping and receiving protocols, where her experience would be valuable. She is also encouraged to pursue professional development opportunities in the field of collections management.

---

**Performance Review — Review Period: 2016-01-01 to 2016-12-31**
**Review Date:** 2017-02-22
**Reviewer:** Director of Collections
**Overall Rating:** Meets Expectations

Clara has had a productive year, successfully managing the relocation of 214 objects from the North Wing Gallery to the newly renovated East Storage Room. This move required careful coordination with the conservation department and the facilities team, and Clara's planning ensured that all objects were moved without damage and that location records were updated in the database within three business days of the move.

She also processed 38 incoming and outgoing loan requests during the year, maintaining accurate files for each transaction. Her communication with borrowing institutions has been professional and clear. Clara is encouraged to continue developing her supervisory skills, as she will be expected to provide guidance to the new Conservation Assistant when that position is filled.

**Review Date:** 2018-02-20

**Overall Rating:** Exceeds Expectations

Clara has taken on additional responsibilities this year with the retirement of the Assistant Registrar. She assumed responsibility for the management of the museum's incoming loan files and has maintained them to the same high standard as the outgoing loan files. She also led the implementation of a new barcode system for tracking object locations, working with the Digital Collections department to integrate the system with the existing database.

Her work on the exhibition "Furniture of the Federal Period" was particularly noteworthy. Clara coordinated the condition reporting for all 47 objects in the exhibition and worked with the curatorial team to resolve two questions of provenance that arose during the installation. Her ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining accuracy has been impressive. Clara is encouraged to consider applying for the Assistant Registrar position when it is formally posted.

---

**Performance Review — Review Period: 2018-01-01 to 2018-12-31**
**Review Date:** 2019-02-19
**Reviewer:** Director of Collections
**Overall Rating:** Exceeds Expectations

Clara was promoted to the position of Assistant Registrar in March of this year, and she has continued to perform at a high level. She has taken on a greater role in the supervision of the registration interns and has provided them with clear guidance and constructive feedback. Her management of the museum's insurance program, including the annual renewal of the fine arts policy, was completed without error.
